audit_context.scope: Read-only web research into Valve update guidance, compatibility and performance; no game files or machine settings modified.
audit_context.date_handling: Converted Unix timestamps to EDT. Forum relative date labels and tracker display timezones were not used as absolute dates.

official_release.title: City Never Sleeps
official_release.retrieval: Verified the landing page using web search and fetched its English localization JavaScript from Valve's official host. Verified announcement date with Steam's public news API.
confirmed_changes: The map and neutral creatures received a substantial visual update.
The engine moved to a newer Source 2 version, with anti-cheat and network prediction work.
Valve describes rendering, audio and trooper performance improvements.
Hero drop shadows now point directly downward; Valve says this improves performance and tracking.
More player settings now persist in the cloud and separate players sharing a PC can retain different settings.
New settings preview/reset tools and configurable health bar displays are available.
official_release.performance_claim_limit: Valve does not quantify FPS gains or provide hardware-specific benchmark results in these update notes.

subsequent_official_updates.title: Forum hotfix after City Never Sleeps
subsequent_official_updates.observations: The latest public reply documents health bar position/name/color changes, bell minimap ping, Down Dash rebind and UI audio adjustments. It does not document a rendering performance fix.

subsequent_official_updates.title: Listen up, Crumbums! Your King is here.
subsequent_official_updates.observations: Steam's official announcement feed confirms Rat King availability. This announcement contains no cache deletion or FPS tuning directive.

yoshi_guidance.direct_discord_access: Original Discord message pages were inaccessible through web.run. Content below is corroborated by two independent community archives, not independently read while logged into the official Discord.

messages.summary: Yoshi said performance fixes were planned for daily updates.
messages.status: Corroborated archive evidence; future work, not proof an FPS fix already shipped.

messages.summary: Yoshi directed users with Rat King camera issues to check their mods.
messages.context: Nearby replies in the second archive concern incorrect camera/FOV behavior.

messages.summary: In a reply to the camera/mod announcement, Yoshi said an alternate fix was being worked on so users would not need to change settings.
messages.status: Observed in DeadVision archive; not a claim the fix already shipped.

exact_delete_all_mods_cache_vpk_claim.searched: Official public forums, Steam announcements, and developer-message archive queries for mods, cache, vpk and remove.
exact_delete_all_mods_cache_vpk_claim.result: No exact Valve/Yoshi directive to delete all mods, mod cache or VPK files was found. Searches cannot prove no such message exists. The user still explicitly requested a configuration without additional mods.

yoshi_guidance.formal_mod_policy: No current primary-source blanket policy endorsing all configuration changes or guaranteeing anti-cheat acceptance was found. Public notes confirm improved anti-cheat but do not specify every relevant restriction.

performance_regression_evidence.type: Original player bug report; not a Valve diagnosis
performance_regression_evidence.hardware: Intel i5-13600KF, AMD RX 7900 XTX, 32 GB RAM, NixOS/Linux
performance_regression_evidence.observations: Author reports about 134 FPS facing dense city geometry versus 271 FPS facing a simpler view, with similar GPU power. Aggregate Source 2 worker CPU time rose about 54%. Low versus Ultra barely affected dense views, and the effect reproduced with Vulkan and DX11 through DXVK.
performance_regression_evidence.limits: Author identifies no specific engine subsystem. Results were not independently reproduced and may not transfer to this Windows machine.
performance_regression_evidence.design_implication: Benchmark dense city directions and combat separately from empty sandbox views; resolution and shader-quality changes alone may leave a CPU-side ceiling.

performance_regression_evidence.type: Original player bug report predating City Never Sleeps
performance_regression_evidence.observations: Author describes 200-560 ms CPU stalls with an idle GPU, opening-session clustering after backend/cache changes, and partial improvement after removing add-on VPKs. Async shader loading reportedly helped early-session hitches but barely changed steady-state behavior.
performance_regression_evidence.limits: Pre-update, one-system evidence. Proposed pipeline-compilation cause and async setting benefits are hypotheses requiring current-build tests.
performance_regression_evidence.design_implication: Record warm-cache and cold-start behavior separately; automatic routine shader-cache deletion is not a demonstrated FPS optimization.

implementation_recommendations: Respect the requested mod-free scope: ordinary user video settings and accessible configuration variables, without add-on VPKs, DLL injection, launch-time plugin loaders or modified search paths.
Keep the current game's stock camera/FOV settings while Rat King camera compatibility is unresolved.
Classify candidate variables using the installed current build and live console output. Do not treat an old internet cvar list as proof that a variable exists or is writable now.
Preserve official VPK asset packages. Any cleanup should identify user add-ons specifically and quarantine them reversibly; deleting every VPK would remove game assets.
Keep rendering features that communicate combat state unless measured gains justify the readability tradeoff.
Backup settings and restore them with the game closed; verify new per-player/cloud persistence behavior rather than assuming old video.txt locations remain authoritative.
Use Steam's documented file verification if a stock file is suspected corrupt; verification is not evidence all extra mod files disappeared.
Measure FPS, frame-time percentiles and hitches in repeated current-build runs before calling this faster than OptiLock.
remaining_uncertainties: The exact user-recalled delete/mod-cache directive cannot be confirmed without an original accessible message.
Public patch notes may omit daily client hotfixes; installed build identity and current behavior must govern tests.
No research alone can establish a fastest configuration or numerical advantage for the user's machine.
